---
name: edit-in-fframes
description: "Rust/SVG video framework."
applications:
  - id: fframes
    role: primary
---

The pinned upstream version is **v1.2.0**. Its guide and API, design and audio references:
https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes/tree/v1.2.0/skills/fframes-video

fframes renders Rust `svgr!` SVG trees through Skia (Metal on macOS, Vulkan on
Linux/Windows), then encodes through linked libav. The toolchain is not bundled
with Voyager. `cargo install --locked --version 1.2.0 cargo-fframes` installs
the matching generator; `cargo fframes new my-video --yes` creates a project
with matching release dependencies. `--git` instead uses upstream main.

Rust and system codec libraries are required. On macOS the guide lists
pkg-config, ffmpeg, x264, x265, opus, nasm and ninja. Voyager's bundled FFmpeg
does not satisfy the linked-library requirements. Windows needs an FFmpeg 9
shared build, LLVM, `FFMPEG_DIR`, `LIBCLANG_PATH` and its DLL directory on `PATH`.
The first release build downloads/builds native dependencies.

Project commands run through `cargo run --release -- <command>`.
`inspect`, `strip`, `frame` and `render` work headlessly; the CPU backend is
available without a preview window. `preview` opens a native window outside
Voyager. `render -o out/piece.mp4` sets an explicit destination; the default is
`out.mp4`. Transparent output requires an alpha-capable encoder. The x264 feature
requires `libav-agree-gpl`, affecting the renderer binary's license, not the videos.
